name: Rufous-banded Owl
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to venezuela, ecuador, peru, and bolivia
description: Uncommon medium-sized owl found in the subtropical and temperate zones of the Andes from Venezuela to Bolivia. Patterned with rufous, dark brown, and white overall.

name: Bismarck Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Mountains of central new britain (southeastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A relatively distinctive honeyeater, olive-brown overall with a darker cast to the face and obvious pale bare skin surrounding and extending slightly behind the eye. Bill is long and conspicuously downturned.

name: Salvadori's Fig-Parrot
rangeDescription: Northwestern new guinea (eastern shore of cenderawasih bay to cyclops mountains)
description: A medium-sized, chunky parrot of lowland and foothill forest. Green body and crown, yellow-green streaked cheek and a blue patch behind the eye.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Saunders's Gull
rangeDescription: Coastal eastern china; winters south korea and southern japan to northern vietnam
description: Elegant, dark-hooded gull, restricted to coastal East Asia. Small but stout-bodied and long-winged, with a dark bill in all plumages.

name: Brown-fronted Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Northern baluchistan and western himalayas (afghanistan to northern india and nepal)
description: A common mid-sized woodpecker of the Himalayas. Note brownish forehead, dark cheek stripe, distinctive black barring on white back, and white spots on black shoulders and wings.

name: Gansu Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of western china (qinghai and gansu)
description: Small, confusing leaf warbler with olive-yellow upperparts, yellow brow, double wing bars, and a pale crown stripe. Extremely similar to many other small leaf warblers: Pallas’s Leaf Warbler has a brighter yellow brow stripe, and Chinese Leaf Warbler has an incrementally weaker head pattern and a small hook at the rear end of the black eye stripe.

name: Black-crested Coquette
rangeDescription: Gulf slope of southern mexico (veracruz) to eastern costa rica
description: Tiny, insectlike hummingbird of humid tropical forest and edge in foothills and lowlands; infrequently seen. Feeds quietly at all levels in small flowers where could easily be passed off as a big moth or bumblebee (and vice versa).

name: Trocaz Pigeon
rangeDescription: Laurel forest of madeira
description: Endemic to the island of Madeira, where it is largely restricted to native laurel and tree heath forests. Body is largely gray with a purple-pink breast, and a noticeable silvery patch with black streaks on the side of the neck.

name: New Britain Boobook
rangeDescription: New britain (southeastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A small brown owl confined to New Britain with a dark brown head, prominent white eyebrows and throat patch, and orange-yellow eyes. Broad brown chest band contrasts with pale mottled whitish underparts.

name: Gray Emutail
rangeDescription: Humid grassy swamps of eastern madagascar
description: Medium-sized, gray-brown bird with a weird spiky tail. Dull streaking on the back and underparts.

name: Rufous-backed Inca-Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of western peru (west slope of western andes in ancash and upper marañón valley)
description: Beautiful finch-like bird with a small range in the Andes of northwestern Peru. Adult is gray with a chestnut back and wings and a black face and throat.

name: Shear-tailed Gray Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Large black-and-gray flycatcher with a long, forked tail. Forages in the canopy at the edge of montane forests and second growth.

name: Rufous Coucal
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (luzon, polillo, and catanduanes)
description: A large, long-tailed bird of lowland and foothill forest tangles and bamboo in the northern Philippines. Sometimes follows mixed-species flocks.

name: White-banded Tanager
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to northeastern paraguay and campos of eastern and southern brazil
description: Medium-sized, strikingly-plumaged tanager resembling a shrike with its mostly gray coloration, a broad black mask, and a white shoulder patch. Occurs in savanna and grasslands with scattered trees where it can be seen in small groups and sometimes accompanying mixed-species flocks.

name: Tumbes Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid littoral of southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Desert-loving sparrow found only in northwestern Peru and southwestern Ecuador. It has gray underparts, a brown back, a striped head, and a large bill; there is no similar species in its range.

name: Black-hooded Sierra Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of southwestern peru (arequipa) to western bolivia, northern chile, and northwestern argentina
description: Attractive small “finch” that is actually a tanager of the high Andes; found in villages, agricultural terraces, scrubby slopes, and bogs. Associates readily with other small seed-eating birds and in some places is tame and acclimated, begging for food at picnic sites.

name: White-bellied Treepie
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southwestern india (western ghats)
description: A handsome long-tailed inhabitant of the Western Ghats. Black face and white underparts set this species apart from Rufous Treepie.

name: Exclamatory Paradise-Whydah
rangeDescription: Senegal and gambia east through southern mali, northern ivory coast, and northern nigeria to the central african republic, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, south sudan, and ethiopia
description: A nest parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of pytilias. As with other whydahs, breeding males are spectacular and bizarre, whereas non-breeding males and females are drab and inconspicuous.

name: Black-billed Scythebill
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (central bahia) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Medium-sized woodcreeper with a remarkable long, slender decurved bill that it uses to probe holes and crevices for insects. Note the pale throat and heavy streaking on the head and upper breast.

name: Turquoise Dacnis
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of colombia
description: A small tanager that is rare and local in the Andes of Colombia. Beautiful male is patterned in electric cerulean and black with an especially prominent black mask and a staring yellow eye.
